item.title: Reese shines again as Dream down Valkyries to lead WNBA Finals
item.description: Angel Reese produced another dominant display as the Atlanta Dream took a 2-1 lead over the Golden State Valkyries in the WNBA Finals (Kevin C. Cox) Angel Reese produced another dominant all-round display as the Atlanta Dream routed the Golden State Valkyries 97-71 to take a 2-1 lead in the best-of-seven WNBA Finals on Wednesday. Three-time WNBA All-Star and reigning defensive player of the year Reese followed up her 30-point display in game two on Monday to once again lead the Atlanta scoring with 21 points. The 24-year-old also reigned on the defensive end, finishing with 12 rebounds and three steals to neutralize Golden State's offense. Reese was one of five Dream players to finish in double-figures, with Rhyne Howard adding 16 points and Naz Hillmon 15 points. Gabby Williams led Golden State's scoring with 15 points. "We feel good -- we're still pissed that we lost the first game," Reese said afterwards. "We know how good we are; we know our identity. "We're all happy for sure, but it's going to take more. The job is not finished so we're going to keep going," added Reese, who is the only woman in history to record consecutive double-doubles in her first three WNBA Finals games. "It feels good when you're in the finals -- when you can do it at the highest level, this is what I live for," Reese said. Earlier, Reese picked up where she left off in game two, draining a three-pointer to help Atlanta take a 22-12 lead as the first quarter drew to a close. Golden State narrowed the deficit to six points at half-time and drew level at 48-48 early in the third quarter. But Atlanta responded with an 8-0 run to pull clear again, and took a stranglehold on the contest after outscoring Golden State 25-17 in the third to lead by 14 points heading into the final period. Atlanta stretched the lead to 21 points late in the fourth quarter to all but ice the contest and the points kept flowing as the Dream delivered a statement victory. Game four takes place in Atlanta on Saturday. Both teams are chasing a first WNBA title. The Dream have come up empty in three prior trips to the Finals, most recently in 2013. The Valkyries, who last year became the first WNBA expansion franchise to reach the playoffs in their inaugural season, are now contending for the title in their second. rcw/bb

item.title: Dillon Danis provides update on Conor McGregor after injury-ending comeback: ‘He was in a dark place’
item.description: LAS VEGAS, CA - (Photo by Hans Gutknecht/Digital First Media/Los Angeles Daily News via Getty Images) | MediaNews Group via Getty Images Conor McGregor’s long awaied comeback was spoiled by a devasting injury just seconds into his fight at UFC 329 but according to one of his closest friends, “The Notorious” is more determined than ever before to return to action. Dillon Danis, who has counted McGregor as a friend and training partner for several years, offered an update on the Irish superstar as he continues to recover after having ACL reconstruction surgery on his knee. While the nding of his fight with Max Holloway was understandably upsetting, Danis promisis that if anybody can go through that and bounce back it’s the former two-diviison UFC champion. “Obviously after the fight you could only imagine how someone could feel coming [back] afer five years and that happening that fast,” Danis told MMA Fighting’s Mike Heck. “He was in a dark place. Any human being will. I’m not going into details what we talked about because that’s obviously personal but as a human, how would you feel? The biggest comeback and that happens. “Now hiis head’s a lot better. He has a 24/7 nurse with him. He’s doing all the exercises. He’s isolated himself in L.A. doing all the right things for his knee and he’s focused on coming back. There’s something about Conor that [when] he puts his mind towards something, he gets it done. There’s no one that will tell him he’s not fighting again, you’re never going to be the same, all the bullshit that everybody says, when that guy has his head on something it’s blinders” With one fight remaining on his current UFC contract, McGregor has already stated several times that he’s plotting his comeback with hopes to compete again as soon as International Fight Week in 2027, which is typically in July. Obviously nothing has been offered or booked but Danis is fully confident that McGregor is doing everything possible to make that comeback. “He is fosused right now,” Danis said. “I talk to him almost everyday and he’s in a good spot right now and I’m happy to see it.”

item.title: Enes Kanter Freedom, Atlanta Dream share conflicting stories in WNBA Finals seat saga
item.description: Former NBA player turned internet troll Enes Kanter Freedom once again tried to stir up controversy and overshadow the WNBA , but this time it may have backfired. Kanter Freedom alleged the Atlanta Dream denied him courtside seats to Game 3 of the WNBA Finals against the Golden State Valkyries on Wednesday night, but the Dream had a very different story. Kanter Freedom started by saying the “director of security” was “banning him” from his seats that he purchased. The internet provocateur recorded a video call declining a move from his seat, saying he was going to show up courtside. “ATTENTION! Just talked to the director of security, and they are now banning us from our purchased seats,” he wrote on X. “Shame on [WNBA]. I guess they have to escort me out of the building. item.title: Atlanta Dream give Enes Kanter private luxury suite over safety concerns at WNBA Finals
item.description: Photo by Joseph Weiser/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Enes Kanter continues to be a factor in WNBA discourse, with the Atlanta Dream releasing a statement about the former NBA star ahead of Game 3. Enes Kanter, or Enes Kanter Freedom as he is now called, has unexpectedly become a notorious figure within the WNBA this season. The former NBA player has made himself the face of the debate about trans athletes, declaring himself for the draft to challenge the league’s eligibility rules. Kanter has been a huge distraction at times this season, especially when he got into a courtside altercation with Natasha Cloud. So when he announced he would be at Game 3 of the WNBA Finals between the Atlanta Dream and the Golden State Valkyries, a few people were concerned. The Dream addressed the situation before the game in a statement. Read Atlanta Dream’s full statement about Enes Kanter after he raised concerns about his safety The debate about transgender athletes is extremely polarising, to say the least. It is something which people feel deeply about on both sides of the issue. And as Jennifer Sey discovered at the Chase Center, taking a stance like she and Kanter have can lead to some serious confrontation. It isn’t surprising, then, that he reportedly had concerns over his safety. Kanter was expected to be seated courtside for the game, but Atlanta decided to go about it differently. “Enes Kanter Freedom has contacted federal, state and local authorities, the WNBA, the Atlanta Dream and State Farm Arena officials to express concerns about his personal safety during his planned attendance at Game 3 of the WNBA Finals tonight. The safety and security of our guests and team members is our highest priority,” the statement reads. Following consultations with the WNBA, Dream ownership, State Farm Arena leadership and security officials, we have directed Mr. Freedom to watch tonight’s game from a private luxury suite. This arrangement is intended to address his security concerns and help provide a safe and positive experience for him and other guests. “The suite will have additional security and will be his designated viewing location for the game. State police have also assigned an officer to Mr. Freedom at his request.” It will be interesting to hear if the former NBA star says what prompted this request for security after the game. In any case, not having Kanter right by the court does reduce the chances of any potential tense moments during the game. The WNBA has to ensure that the focus remains on basketball. item.title: Booker's 'biggest leap' comments about Maluach fully resonating now
item.description: PORTLAND – Phoenix Suns All-Star Devin Booker’s praise of Khaman Maluach on media day last month confirmed what the 7-footer showed in NBA Summer League. “He's way ahead of the curve just to be going into his second year,” Booker said back in September. “He's asking a lot of questions, but you can tell he's asking them when he already knows the answer and he knows what to do. It's been a pleasure to watch him grow. I'd say he's taken the biggest leap out of anybody that I've seen this summer and with the unfortunate injury to Mark, I think (Maluach is) going to be thrown into the fire a lot more, and we'll get to learn through experience. All these moments matter.” Those comments are resonating even more now. Maluach is getting the start at center in Wednesday night’s season opener Oct. 21 against the Portland Trail Blazers at Moda Center. The 10 th overall pick in the 2025 NBA Draft, the 7-footer Maluach has been battling Oso Ighodaro for the starting center position as Mark Williams will miss multiple months of the season with a left shoulder injury he sustained during an offseason workout. Ighodaro recently signed a three-year, $29-million extension, showing the Suns see him as a long-term investment. Playing every game last season, Ighodaro served as backup to Williams last season. Suns coach Jordan Ott has talked all training camp and preseason about how matchups will factor in who plays. The Blazers start 7-footer Donovan Clingan at center. Clingan led the NBA in offensive rebounds last season at 4.5 a game, but he can also pop out for 3. In his third season, Clingan shot 34.1% (84-of-246) from distance last season. Robert Williams is Portland’s backup center. At 6 feet, 9 inches, Williams isn’t as tall as Clingan, but he too is physical and gets on the offensive boards. Williams averaged 2.4 offensive rebounds a game last season. So when looking at Maluach starting and Ighodaro coming off the bench, matchups appear to have played a role in the decision. At the same, Ott also said he’s not one to change who starts from game to game and wouldn’t want to change unless one was needed. Have opinions about the current state of the Suns? item.title: Atlanta Dream rolls to WNBA Finals win, takes a 2-1 series lead on Golden State
item.description: ATLANTA — Atlanta Dream coach Karl Smesko insisted that a good shooting night was coming for his team. He said it after Game 1, and he repeated the message after Game 2. The coaching staff liked the shot quality Atlanta was getting, even against the Golden State Valkyries’ excellent defense. The shots would start falling. In Game 3, the Dream finally delivered, and the Valkyries couldn’t compete in a shootout. Atlanta took control early, weathered a comeback attempt by Golden State to start the third quarter and cruised in the second half to a 97-71 victory on Wednesday night. The Dream take a 2-1 series lead into Saturday’s Game 4 at State Farm Arena. After shooting below 34 percent in both games in San Francisco, the floodgates opened in Atlanta. The Dream made 49 percent of their field goals and shot 41 percent from beyond the arc. All seven rotation players — excluding those who took the floor during garbage time — scored at least 7 points. Atlanta never trailed after scoring the first six points. Golden State tied the game at 49 in the third quarter, but Rhyne Howard responded with a reverse layup on the ensuing possession and the Dream never looked back. Angel Reese led the way with 21 points and 12 rebounds, and Howard added 16 points for the Dream. Golden State shot only 35 percent, and made just 11 of 17 free throws. item.title: Stephon Castle hopes to avoid falling for Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's foul-drawing
item.description: The mind games continue. Regardless of the result. Circling it for months, the Oklahoma City Thunder absolutely showed up and dominated Opening Night en route to a 116-104 win over the San Antonio Spurs . For the first time in a while, they thoroughly outplayed their archrival. That said, the war continues. Exchanging battle wins, the Thunder and Spurs have faced off a ridiculous 13 times over the last calendar year. That includes an epic seven-game duel in the 2026 Western Conference Finals where OKC fell just shy of back-to-back NBA championships. You can't erase that, but this was a step in the right direction for the Thunder to reshift their narrative. Opening Night was a must-win scenario. For vibes and storylines. Credit to OKC, it played like it was the case. They were the more physical team from the jump. Up by as many as 26 points, they completely stonewalled Victor Wembanyama and company. Now that that's over, the Spurs are looking ahead. As of now, the Thunder only face them two more times in the 2026-27 regular season — Feb. 11 and Mar. 14. So we're a little ways away from a potential new chapter. That said, Stephon Castle is getting ready already. For the first time in a while, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander absolutely cooked Castle. The two-time MVP winner had 32 points on 13-of-27 shooting, six rebounds and four assists. He shot 3-of-7 from 3 and went 3-of-4 on free throws. Anytime the Thunder desperately needed a bucket to slow down San Antonio's run, he answered the call. The two most important numbers there? Gilgeous-Alexander's low free-throw attempts and high 3-point volume. Perhaps he's shifting more toward a jumper-happy scorer. The drives to the rim were down. The 28-year-old may be trying to be more cognizant of saving his legs for the 2027 NBA playoffs. But Castle went at Gilgeous-Alexander's contact selling. Even though the numbers don't reflect a huge free-throw shooting game. "Really trying to be physical with him, but physical enough to where you don't bait yourself into a foul. That's probably the hardest part," Castle said. "But it's not really an individual thing, it's more of a team thing. That goes for any good player in the league." This is all mind games from Castle and the Spurs. If you follow the NBA long enough, you know teams usually make these comments for the next game. We'll see if it works out, but Gilgeous-Alexander's free-throw numbers were a non-storyline on Opening Night. Stephon Castle on the challenge of guarding SGA: "Really trying to be physical with him, but physical enough to where you don't bait yourself into a foul. That's probably the hardest part. But it's not really an individual thing, it's more of a team thing" pic.twitter.com/wbH2hS5UF3 — Oh No He Didn't 🤯 (@ohnohedidnt24) October 21, 2026 This article originally appeared on OKC Thunder Wire: Stephon Castle hopes to avoid falling for Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's foul-drawing

item.title: Bayern Munich boss Vincent Kompany explains bizarre lineup vs. Arsenal
item.description: Bayern Munich's English forward #09 Harry Kane (R) and Bayern Munich's Canadian defender #19 Alphonso Davies come out to warm up prior to the UEFA Champions League football match between FC Bayern Munich and Arsenal FC in Munich, southern Germany on October 21, 2026. (Photo by Karl-Josef HILDENBRAND / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany knew it would surprise some folks when he deployed Alphonso Davies at left wing against Arsenal, but the decision came after close consultation with club higher-ups. With Luis Díaz a major doubt, Michael Olise suspended, Joshua Kimmich mourning t he passing of his father, and Jamal Musiala unavailable, FC Bayern had to get creative with its attacking options. Nathaniel Brown was also considered for the role, but Kompany and the club’s leadership ultimately settled on Davies as an alternative. Kompany explained the thinking behind the decision. “Lucho was a major doubt, Michael wasn’t there. Jamal wasn’t there. We considered using Nene Brown in attack. We knew we had Phonzy as an option in situations like today, we know he can help us in that position. We spoke about that in discussions with Max (Eberl) and Christoph (Freund). We have enough defenders at the moment. That’s why we decided to use him there. We knew a moment like this would come at some point, and we used it.” The decision reflects the Bavarians’ confidence in Davies’ versatility and attacking qualities. With defensive options available, Kompany saw an opportunity to use the Canadian international further forward when FC Bayern needed solutions. However, the lineup also created issues in certain positions that did not work out in the end (such as Josip Stanišić’s disaster class at left-back). item.title: Miami scores big recruiting win after flipping 4-star LB
item.description: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Miami scores big recruiting win after flipping 4-star LB appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Miami Hurricanes scored a big win on the recruiting trail Wednesday by flipping four-star linebacker Aston Whiteside from the Texas A&M Aggies, adding another blue-chip prospect to their 2027 class. The Burleson, Texas, native announced his decision on social media after visiting Miami for its home game against Florida State last weekend. Whiteside had been committed to Texas A&M since June 1, shortly after taking an official visit to the Aggies. However, the Hurricanes continued pursuing the linebacker after offering him during the offseason, eventually convincing him to change his commitment. The 6-foot-2 prospect, listed at 205 pounds, is the No. 27 linebacker and No. 347 overall player in the 2027 recruiting class, according to 247Sports’ composite rankings. Rivals ranks him No. 21 among linebackers and No. 254 nationally, while the Rivals industry ranking places him at No. 31 among linebackers and No. 376 overall. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Whiteside has built a statistically impressive body of work during his high school career. Last season, he finished with 46 tackles, three tackles for loss and one forced fumble. This year, he has accumulated 91 tackles, 11 tackles for loss, four sacks and a forced fumble, along with a punt-return touchdown. Whiteside, whose father also played in the NFL and Canadian Football League, joins fellow blue-chip linebackers AJ Randle Jr. and Noah Glover in Miami’s 2027 class, giving the Hurricanes three highly regarded prospects at the position. Miami entered Wednesday with the nation’s No. 3 recruiting class and now has 21 commitments in the 2027 cycle. Meanwhile, for Texas A&M, the loss of Whiteside comes as a setback for its highly ranked recruiting class. The Aggies still have 24 commitments, including five-star linebacker Kaden Henderson and four-star linebacker Mikahi Allen. Texas A&M also leads the country with five commitments from five-star prospects. item.title: CF Montréal fall to Forge FC in Canadian Championship final
item.description: CF Montréal fall to Forge FC in Canadian Championship final By Dylan Butler CF Montréal fell to Forge FC 4-2 on penalty kicks in the 2026 Canadian Championship final after the teams played to a 1-1 deadlock through 120 minutes on Wednesday night at Stade Saputo. It was CF Montréal's ninth trip to the CanChamp final, and first since lifting the Voyageurs Cup in 2021. Meanwhile, Forge, who eliminated Montréal from the Canadian Championship for a third straight year, became the first Canadian Premier League team to win the title and clinched a berth in the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup . CF Montréal had a golden chance to take an early lead when leading scorer Prince Owusu stepped up to take a penalty kick. But Forge goalkeeper Dimitry Bertaud denied the Ghanaian striker, diving to his left to save the PK. Instead, Forge entered halftime with the advantage. Antoine Batisse latched onto Noah Jensen's corner kick at the near post and headed past Montréal goalkeeper Sébastian Breza deep into first-half stoppage time. Four minutes into the second half, CFMTL leveled through Daniel Ríos , who headed in from the edge of the six-yard box. The hosts were reduced to 10 men in the 54th minute when Brayan Vera was sent off for his second bookable offense. Bertaud was the hero during the shootout, making two more saves for Forge before Manjrekar James clinched the CPL side's historic win in the fifth round. item.title: Brady Bowl: Ottawa Senators Get Revenge on Tkachuk, Panthers
item.description: Brady Tkachuk got an expected response in his return to Ottawa with the Florida Panthers on Wednesday, but it was the Senators who really enjoyed the homecoming game. The Senators rallied from a 1-0 lead — which was supplied by Tkachuk — and rolled to a 5-1 win, snapping the Panthers’ three-game winning streak. The game ended with Brady in the Florida room after a scrum in the final minutes as trash, jerseys, and other debris hit the ice. The Panthers visit the Pittsburgh Penguins on Thursday. Tkachuk was booed from warmups on, with some vocal Ottawa fans throating an obscene chant throughout the game . Yet, not long after Tkachuk’s tribute video, he gave the Panthers a 1-0 lead on a power-play feed from older brother Matthew . The rest of the night belonged to the Senators. Ottawa tied the score on a Tim Stutzle power-play goal toward the end of the first, then added two more in the second. Linus Ullmark made 16 saves for the Senators before having to be helped off the ice at 3:35 of the third period after making a kick save. Samuel Ersson came on for the Sens, and it did not matter much. Florida failed to get off a single shot before Warren Foegele made it 4-1 about 3 minutes later. Brady Tkachuk played 13:13 of the game, taking three penalties. He was a minus-2. GAMEDAY NOTES: PANTHERS at SENATORS Brady Tkachuk became the fourth player to score at least seven goals through their first 10 career games with the Panthers, following Pavel Bure (10 in 1998-99), Ray Whitney (seven in 1997-98) and Ray Sheppard (seven in 1995-96). The seven goals scored in the first 10 games of a season is tied for fourth-most by a Panthers player in their history. Aside from the ones listed above, Sam Reinhart had eight in 2023, and Scott Mellanby had eight in 1995. Matthew Tkachuk continued his point streak to nine games after assisting on Brady’s first period goal. Matthew has had a point in all but Florida’s 1-0 OT win at Carolina in the opener. HOW THEY SCORED Panthers 1, Senators 0 (10:00 1st PP): Who else but Brady Tkachuk , eh? Brady gets along the goal line, takes a pass from Matthew and powers a shot past Linus Ullmark . Senators 1, Panthers 1 (14:13 1st PP): Tim Stutzle evens things up by drilling a one-timer from the right circle through Akira Schmid . Senators 2, Panthers 1 (9:32 2nd): Claude Giroux rips one through from the slot. Senators 3, Panthers 1 (17:18 2nd): Shane Pinto gets loose and, despite being wrapped up by Niko Mikkola , slides a shot home. Senators 4, Panthers 1 (7:58 3rd): Warren Foegele whips one from the slot to all but finish this thing. Senators 5, Panthers 1 (14:57 3rd): Stephen Halliday one-times a drop pass from Stutzle for good measure. FHN’S 3 STARS 1. Tim Stutzle, Senators 2. Shane Pinto, Senators 3. item.title: Watch Kevin Durant posterize Cooper Flagg on emphatic slam dunk
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images Watch Kevin Durant posterize Cooper Flagg on emphatic slam dunk appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . No more internet lobs for now from Houston Rockets star Kevin Durant this time. The Rockets forward is back to business on the court with the 2026-27 NBA season finally here, and he already has a poster dunk . He took off and threw down an emphatic dunk right in front of Dallas Mavericks forward Cooper Flagg in a season-opening game at Toyota Center in Houston on Wednesday. Here is that huge dunk from Durant on the Mavs youngster, and it surely deserves multiple replays. It was that good. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) KEVIN DURANT ROCKS THE RIM WITH THIS EMPHATIC SLAM 😤 pic.twitter.com/Y72AVIycHh — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) October 22, 2026 Durant easily got by the defense of Mavericks forward PJ Washington and drove down the lane with barely any resistance there from Dallas. Flagg was the last man on defense for the Mavs, but he didn’t even bother to jump and challenge Durant at the rim. He knew what was going to be the outcome with the former NBA Most Valuable Player coming down the lane with full force. Durant is still a problem for opposing defenses. His blend of length, range and mobility remain a dangerous mix, and he showed that in that play. Durant could have just pulled up for a 3-pointer there, as Washington wasn’t really all over him, but he saw an open lane and decided to attack it. Now in his 20th season in the league, Durant is looking to lead the Rockets to the top, while he still can play at a high level. That is going to be easier said than done, but Houston has the talent to make the NBA Playoffs and make a deep posteason run. But that’s a long way from now, with Rockets focusing more at the moment in winning early momentum in the season. item.title: Exhi Observations: Kansas
item.description: College basketball exhibitions are a new gadget and exactly how to deal with them is in its nascent stage. For players. For coaching staffs. Most certainly for fan bases, who still seem to be having great difficulty grasping the reality that games such as Louisville vs. Kansas in The Phog on October 21 is Milwaukee Brewers vs Tampa Bay Devil Rays . . . . . . in Phoenix, Arizona on March 4. Which is not to deny I didn’t get a bit nervous during the day. Or that I didn’t take notes during the game, if not nearly as detailed as a game that counts. Or that my heart rate didn’t quicken at crunch time. Some random takeaways. * * * * * Obinna Ekezie Jr. At the practice media were allowed to attend last week, he drained triple after triple after triple. We now have a sense that wasn’t an aberration. He is long long long and for somebody who should still be playing in HS understands for the most part how to use that on D. It’s a revelation. He just about single handedly secured U of L’s command of the contest after the Cards took the lead with a boffo start to the 2d. Obi blocked Jayhawk shots on consecutive possessions. Then drained a triad of treys in a couple minute span. Still rounding into full fettle from his injuries, he netted four threeballs. blocked a team leading five shots, and grabbed a team leading 8 rebounds. Red & Black Nation, meet Obi Ekezie Jr. * * * * * The first half numbers of U of L’s heralded first TP gets were bracing. C Flory Bidunga had nary a rebound in the first half. PG Jackson Shelstad had nary an assist in the first half. FB’s propensity to foul — on display last year — came with him from Lawrence. He didn’t get a board until ten minutes were left to play and he snared a short armed jumper and got a put back. He only grabbed three total, but one secured the game on a missed Seth Trimble FT at 1:29. His D was solid, but his total game was off. Shelstad finished with a team high 23 points. and a lone assist. My guess is Trimble will evolve as the main PGish guy. * * * * * De’Shayne Montgomery, of whom we have spoken little, was and shall continue to be Solid. Adrian Wooley shall be a factor. His consecutive threes on the second and third possessions after halftime kickstarted the Cardinals. Louisville’s backcourt as presently constituted is a force. * * * * * Alvaro Folgueiras is a key piece to this puzzle. My guess is he’ll be getting the ball up top like Aly Khalifa. He is a very good and astute passer. He tied for the team lead with four assists. When his mates get to know his tendencies better that number shall rise. His was a steady if not highlight reel presence throughout. * * * * * Bench points: Louisville 35, Kansas 13. Nice. Fast break points: Louisville 8, Kansas 26. Not nice. Paint points: Louisville 20, Kansas 40. Naughty and and not nice. * * * * * Louisville’s ball movement was, how to say it, just about non existent. item.title: Clippers to start season with several notable players out
item.description: The Los Angeles Clippers will start the season with several notable players absent to start the season. The team’s initial injury report for the season opener against the Kings on Wednesday, Oct. 21 featured five players ruled out. Brandon Ingram will be the biggest absence for the team, considering he would’ve been a potential starter and was one of the primary trade assets in the package sent over by the Toronto Raptors for Kawhi Leonard during the offseason. Ingram was named an All-Star last season before finishing with 77 starts for the Raptors last season. He averaged 21.5 points, 5.6 rebounds and 3.7 assists. He is recovering from right heel surgery he had in May. He is also dealing with a partially torn Achilles tendon. A timetable has not been set for Ingram’s return. Max Strus is another new addition to the roster who will miss time to start the season. He suffered a right plantar fascia partial tear during a preseason game against the Golden State Warriors in Hawaii on Oct. 4. He was initially seen limping back to the locker room after he tried to cut across the top of the key to receive a pass from guard Darius Garland during the first quarter. Strus was acquired in August as part of a multi-team trade that involved the Cleveland Cavaliers , Denver Nuggets and Washington Wizards . Yanic Konan Niederhauser and Bradley Beal are among the returns on the injury report. Konan Niederhäuser, Beal, Ingram and Strus are making progress in their recovery but are not expected to travel with the team to Oklahoma City. The Clippers will play the Los Angeles Lakers on Friday, Oct. 23, before traveling to play the Oklahoma City Thunder on Sunday, Oct. 25. item.title: Just $10 Million Stands In Way Of Colts Trading Jonathan Taylor
item.description: Jonathan Taylor #28 of the Indianapolis Colts celebrates after his team's 38-14 victory against the Tennessee Titans. Getty The Indianapolis Colts just signed Jonathan Taylor to a contract extension in the offseason. There was likely no world where they considered that he might become a trade candidate after just six weeks of the season. But that’s what has happened. There are calls left and right for the Colts to at least consider trading Taylor. Usually, a player on a fresh contract extension is particularly difficult to trade, though. There’s a lot of years and money remaining on the new deal, and a new team doesn’t always want to take that on. Taylor’s extension actually makes him rather tradeable, which could turn out to be a key detail in what happens next with the Colts and their superstar running back. How Jonathan Taylor’s Contract Impacts Trade Taylor’s extension was for just two years, so right off the bat that’s easier to deal with than a longer-term deal. And the way the Colts set up the money actually does them a bunch of favors. “If, hypothetically, someone wanted to trade for Taylor, the recency of the extension doesn’t make it impossible for the Colts to move him, as it might in the case of some other extensions,” ESPN’s Dan Graziano wrote in a new article on Wednesday . “The Colts would have to account for $10 million of additional dead money accelerating onto their 2027 salary cap as a result of the signing bonus proration that remains. His 2026 salary is $6.98 million, so an acquiring team would be responsible for whatever percentage of that remains, plus $60,000 for each remaining game in the form of fully guaranteed per-game roster bonuses. If a team with 11 games remaining in its season were to trade for Taylor today, that team would be on the hook for about $5.3 million for 2026. Taylor is scheduled to earn another $16.02 million in 2027. None of the 2027 money is currently guaranteed, but it all becomes guaranteed five days after the Super Bowl.” The relevant thing for fans to know is that a lot of superstar contracts are a lot tougher to move than Taylor’s would be. They often come with larger dead money cap hits, and the longer remaining on a deal, the more complicated it can be. As far as Taylor’s contract is concerned, he’s quite moveable. What Jonathan Taylor Trade Would Mean If the Colts really ended up trading Taylor, it would change the complexion of their future. It would be one of the fullest steps into a rebuild that Indy could undertake. You only trade away the stud running back if you don’t plan on being competitive for at least a couple of years. A Taylor trade might be preceded, or followed, by deals away of DeForest Buckner , and Quenton Nelson, and Josh Downs — players all on expiring contracts. There are moves the Colts can make to go halfway here. Trading Taylor wouldn’t be one of them. That’d be a total press of the reset button. item.title: ‘A complete threat’: Rio Ngumoha’s electric display excites Van Dijk and Liverpool
item.description: Teenager produced man-of-the-match performance against Villarreal and has learned from Salah, says Reds captain The shot sailed wide of Peter Gulacsi’s top corner and into the Kop, affording Villarreal much-needed respite at 4-2, but for Andoni Iraola it was a standout moment in a scintillating Champions League display from Rio Ngumoha. To a coach who called for versatility from all of his wingers this summer, here was a significant step forward among many from the 18-year-old at Anfield. There were questions over how Ngumoha would adapt to playing on the right even before Liverpool increased the likelihood by signing Bradley Barcola for £123m from Paris Saint-Germain. On his fifth start under Iraola on Tuesday, which his side won 4-3 , Liverpool witnessed an answer: quickly, incisively and confidently. The teenager’s willingness to cut inside from the right and shoot from distance with his left foot captured Iraola’s imagination as much as the devastating run that created Alexis Mac Allister’s second goal of the game. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.description: Phil Foden shouted the loudest on a quiet night at the Etihad Stadium, announcing his personal return to form with an instinctive hat-trick as Manchester City dispatched AEK Athens with little fuss. Enzo Maresca had called for City to make their own noise amid the cacophony around the club but a businesslike victory in front of 20,000 fewer than watched the weekend’s win over Ipswich was required to get their Champions League back on track after suffering at the hands of Paris Saint-Germain . Those in attendance, officially 40,042 but that felt optimistic, saw Foden shine on the right wing and as a central striker, showing there is life without Erling Haaland, who watched from the bench. Admittedly, the opposition were not a match for the Premier League side, whose other goals came from Elliot Anderson and Rayan Cherki. Stavros Pilios’s consolation was more a reward for the boisterous fans in yellow and black, who created the atmosphere, than for the overall efforts of the visitors. Continue reading...

item.description: As Tottenham edged to victory over Coventry , a familiar face among the post-match salutations. Could that be Dejan Kulusevski? For it was he, playing 526 days since his last Spurs appearance. Much has changed though still much stays the same. Ben Davies’s deflected late clincher catapulted Spurs up to … 16th. When Kulusevski last played on 11 May 2025, Tottenham were 17th, the position in which they finished both that season and in 2025-26. Further to Peters and Lee [ Monday’s Football Daily letters] another 70s example that occurred to me was the West Ham players Mervyn Day and Bill Green . They were both in the West Ham United team from 1976-78, and in Carlisle United’s greatest season 1974-75. When Green was still at Carlisle, he played against West Ham’s Day. So plenty of Green Day commentary opportunities there. Of course, the band hadn’t formed yet, but who knows, perhaps they thought of the band’s name whilst watching some old 70s football footage” – Bob Dunning. On the subject of musical football matchups, all I can say is that it’s just a shame Gareth Barry was at Manchester City a few years too late to play alongside David White ” – Tim Russell. Such was the style of play, it did introduce a some element of entertainment into our visits to the old stadium” – Tommy Boyd (and, surprisingly, others). His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.description: Defender may not be blameless in team’s struggles but his criticism goes to the heart of what has gone wrong at the club Heartbreaking: the worst defender you know just made a great point. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. item.title: The Premier League so far: draws, underperforming xG and other data pointers
item.description: Goal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and forwards underperform against xG Goals are on the up in the Premier League. The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
